REA itself offers both CLI and MCP interfaces, so this benchmark does not establish that LeanREA replaces all REA workflows.

The pinned project declares MIT for its skill and benchmark code and credits REA’s code and documentation for many workflow details; it explicitly disclaims affiliation. External analysis tools, model services and target applications retain separate requirements and terms. The benchmark document is dated 2026-10-16; the initial public commit is dated 2026-10-17, and only the README changed before the reviewed pin. This collection inspected source and recomputed published metric totals without running the skill, models, tools or targets.

name: UU Remote on Linux: an unofficial protocol implementation
description_en: Implements an unofficial native Linux host for NetEase UU Remote, using protocol behavior the maintainer says was recovered from official-client traffic and shipped programs. The Rust implementation connects selected desktop, input and auxiliary-tool channels to Linux services; an additional Linux viewer remains experimental. The author attributes development to Claude and Codex, without establishing REA use.
description_zh: 实现网易 UU 远程的非官方原生 Linux 被控端；维护者称协议行为来自对官方客户端流量及已发布程序的调查。Rust 实现将选定的桌面、输入和辅助工具通道连接到 Linux 服务，另有仍处于实验阶段的 Linux 控制端。作者将开发归因于 Claude 与 Codex，未确立 REA 使用。
requirements: Reviewed version 0.2.8 implements selected protocol formats and session behavior in native Rust with small C components, without Wine or bundled NetEase binaries. The additional Linux viewer is experimental. Cargo.toml declares GPL-3.0-or-later; dependencies and official clients/services retain separate terms. This is not recovered vendor source or a replacement cloud backend.

The host needs Linux, stable Rust, a C toolchain, pkg-config, X11 development libraries and FFmpeg. GTK3 supports graphical login; the optional viewer also needs SDL2. Wayland/portal builds require additional libraries and authorized desktop access. Dependencies vary by feature; arbitrary Linux compatibility is not established.

UU cloud services remain required; the host and experimental viewer interoperate with supported official clients and hosts. Account connections use the user’s own authorized account; experimental remote assistance requires an explicitly enabled host and recipient-provided connection details. The project is unaffiliated with NetEase, and no security audit or complete protocol equivalence is established.

Public parsing and initialization code has synthetic checks for malformed inputs, capability replies and echo correlation. Local/virtual WebRTC peers test pending-desktop responses, independent tool connections and session isolation. These are implementation checks, not an independent official-client conformance corpus. This entry is source-reviewed; tests and device behavior were not independently run.

The README reports real-machine GNOME/X11 use and selected GNOME Wayland checks; other desktop coverage is largely virtual-machine based. Its viewer acceptance matrix is explicitly partial, with different official-host coverage for clipboard, audio, codecs and keyboards. These remain author-reported observations, not generally applicable compatibility results.

Wayland remains experimental, with single-screen and resolution/recovery limits. Multi-monitor switching is under development; HDR, privacy-screen mode, microphone forwarding and the Linux pre-login screen are unsupported. Restrictive-network relay behavior is not thoroughly tested. Cloud behavior and supported versions may change independently of this snapshot.

name: Perfect Dark: matching Nintendo 64 decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs Perfect Dark’s Nintendo 64 code with a documented matching-ROM build. The project combines reconstructed source with assets from a user-supplied original ROM, then checks version-specific artifact hashes. It is a reproducible-build research case, distinct from the separate native PC port; matching results remain project-reported here.
description_zh: 重建 Perfect Dark 的 Nintendo 64 代码，并提供生成一致 ROM 的构建流程。项目将重建源码与使用者自备原 ROM 中的素材结合，再检查各版本产物的哈希。这是可复现构建研究案例，与独立的原生 PC 移植不同；此处的一致性结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: The reviewed GitHub repository mirrors Ryan Dwyer’s GitLab project. README describes a complete matching decompilation; six build targets cover NTSC beta, NTSC 1.0/final, PAL beta/final and Japanese final, with ntsc-final as default. This reconstructs an N64 ROM, not a Windows/Linux/macOS game executable or the separate Perfect Dark PC port.

Supply an independently authorized original ROM in non-byteswapped .z64 form, with header 0x80371240, named for the selected ROMID. make extract reads assets and comparison segments from that ROM; final builds also reuse extracted boot code. Existing extracted files are not overwritten, so modified inputs can invalidate matching results.

The documented host setup is Linux: GNU Make, host C/C++ tools, Python 3, MIPS binutils/GCC, armips, Capstone development files and the listed 32-bit libc headers. Initialize the pinned ido-static-recomp submodule. Matching mode reconstructs IDO 5.3 and 7.1 compiler tools from its IRIX inputs; optional GCC builds are nonmatching and limited to ntsc-1.0/ntsc-final.

After building, make test runs quiet MD5 verification against the selected version’s checksum manifest, including the final ROM and intermediate artifacts. The README also documents comparing base/built ROM hashes. These check output identity for the supplied version, not gameplay-path coverage or performance. The mutable status page reports all six versions complete/matching; this collection did not rerun those checks.

The repository declares MIT for source; original ROMs and extracted game assets retain separate rights. Compiler components have their own terms, including the submodule’s SGI notice for IDO 5.3; the project’s MIT declaration does not replace them. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: TCLimate: reconstructing selected TCL Home cloud controls
description_en: Implements selected TCL Home air-conditioner controls and electricity reporting in a native macOS menu-bar app. It adapts earlier community protocol work and documents an Android-module investigation to recover a separate statistics request. Reported validation checks cloud state, not independent physical operation or complete device equivalence.
description_zh: 在原生 macOS 菜单栏应用中实现选定的 TCL Home 空调控制与用电量报告。项目改编既有社区协议实现，并记录通过调查 Android 模块恢复另一条统计请求的过程。报告的验证检查云端状态，不等于独立核实设备实际运行或完整设备等价性。
requirements: Reviewed v0.1.6 beta requires macOS 14+, internet access and a TCL account with already-paired ACs. Building needs Swift 6.0+, Xcode Command Line Tools and a persistent signing certificate for the packaged app. Pairing still uses TCL Home; local LAN control and direct Google sign-in are absent.

The protocol implementation credits nemesa’s MIT-licensed Home Assistant integration. The electricity API was reportedly identified through Android Flutter-module inspection and a successful request capture; original packages, captures and detailed investigation logs are not included in the repository. The inspected repository does not establish the collection report’s REA/mitmproxy attribution.

Source guards commands using reported model/state fields, restricts target temperature to whole degrees from 16–30°C, and checks reported state after sending. Optimistic UI changes are not themselves confirmation; unsuccessful confirmation is marked. Extra controls depend on available fields and modes, rather than assuming every AC supports them.

Author validation covers a Pakistan account and two Split AC-1 units: authentication, discovery, reported state, power, temperature and daily electricity. Modes, fan, airflow and other optional controls lack physical validation; other regions/models remain unverified. Cloud confirmation does not independently establish airflow or compressor operation.

Energy parsing preserves genuine zeros, excludes invalid readings and leaves missing days as gaps; a seven-day total requires all seven readings. No persistent energy history or cost estimate is implemented. Offline tests are reported but absent from the reviewed tree/package targets. This source review did not run tests or devices.

MIT covers project code, with attribution retained for the earlier integration. Official services and third-party material retain separate terms. This is an unofficial cloud-dependent client, not recovered TCL source or firmware; APIs may change independently of the app.

name: Universal Modder
description_en: Packages agent skills, three role briefs, a Python CLI and preconfigured fal MCP settings for modding PC games the user owns. Its reverse-engineering guidance sends managed, native and data-format work to external decompilers and debuggers, and requires a round-trip check before a reverse-engineered file format is used; one worked example ships an Age of Empires II sprite writer built this way. It is a modding toolkit with agent-written field notes, not a game decompilation, and its example results remain project-reported.
description_zh: 为修改用户自有的 PC 游戏打包智能体技能、三份角色说明、Python 命令行工具及预配置的 fal MCP 设置。其逆向分析指南把托管代码、原生代码和数据格式工作交给外部反编译器与调试器，并要求逆向得到的文件格式先通过往返检查再投入使用；其中一个示例附带按此方法实现的 Age of Empires II 精灵写入器。它是附带智能体实践笔记的模组工具包，不是游戏反编译重建，示例结果仍为项目报告。
requirements: The reviewed pin is Python package version 0.2.0. It ships twelve Agent Skills-format skills, three subagent role files, the um CLI and per-client settings for the hosted fal MCP server, with install routes for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code/Copilot, Cursor and OpenCode. The host needs Git, Python 3.10+ and ffmpeg, with uv recommended and Blender only for 3D-to-sprite rendering; Windows capture, input and launch commands run natively or from WSL.

Work starts from a game installation the user owns. The toolkit supplies no game files, ROMs or decompiled code, and tells agents to keep decompiles and extracted assets outside the repository. Asset generation needs a fal API key or fal’s browser sign-in; a local ComfyUI server is an image alternative, and Sprixen is a separate paid API. Decompilers, debuggers, loaders and MCP servers named in the skills, such as ILSpy, Cpp2IL, Ghidra, IDA, Cheat Engine, Frida and RenderDoc, are installed separately.

The reverse-engineering skill asks agents to read decompiled code, data or live memory, confirm guesses dynamically, and prove a reverse-engineered file format with a decode–encode–decode round trip before writing new files. It reports that the Age of Empires II DE .sld writer was accepted at 0.9/255 mean error on a stock sprite, and that a ported Terraria boss-movement rule matched recorded velocities at 99.9%. The AoE2 example reports in-game testing in September 2026; these are author results, not reproduced here.

Repository CI runs the Python tests, every CLI help screen, a knowledge-base index check and a publish lint that blocks game files, decompiled code and secrets. These checks cover the toolkit, not whether a mod works in a particular game. Knowledge-base field notes are agent-written and PR-reviewed with self-declared status and verification sections; they are not independently verified compatibility records. This collection reviewed source and documentation without running the CLI, skills, games or examples.

Project rules limit work to games the user owns, offline or on servers the user hosts, and refuse injection into anti-cheat-protected online clients, cheats against other players, and DRM, anti-cheat or ownership-check bypasses. The repository declares MIT for its code and bundles fonts under the SIL OFL; generated assets follow fal and model terms, and games, loaders and external tools keep their own terms. Its safety notes cite takedowns of projects that shipped no assets. The reviewed sources establish no REA connection.

name: Browserbase plugin: re-hosting Claude in Chrome’s browser bridge
description_en: Stands in for the Claude in Chrome extension side of Claude Code’s local browser bridge and runs the requested actions in Browserbase cloud browsers. The author’s thread describes the reverse-engineered framing, a 4-byte little-endian length before each JSON tool call, and the plugin maps 17 named tools onto Stagehand/CDP operations. It is an archived interoperability shim with several placeholder tools, not recovered Anthropic code or a verified equivalent of the extension.
description_zh: 在 Claude Code 本地浏览器桥接中替代 Claude in Chrome 扩展一端，把请求的操作交给 Browserbase 云端浏览器执行。作者的帖子串描述了逆向得到的消息格式，即每条 JSON 工具调用前加 4 字节小端长度；插件则将 17 个具名工具映射为 Stagehand／CDP 操作。这是已归档的互操作适配层，部分工具仅为占位实现，并非恢复出的 Anthropic 代码，也未经验证与扩展等价。
requirements: The reviewed main branch is archived, and its commits are dated 2025-12-27. A SessionStart hook launches a Node forwarding server that moves any existing claude-mcp-browser-bridge-<user> socket in the temporary directory aside and listens in its place. Messages carry a 4-byte little-endian length plus JSON; only the execute_tool method is accepted, with 17 named tool handlers and errors for anything else.

Requires Claude Code with plugin support, the Claude in Chrome extension, Node.js 18+, the Browserbase SDK and Stagehand npm packages, and a Browserbase API key and project ID. As written, the start hook looks for the extension only under the macOS Chrome profile directory and stops when it is missing, so other hosts fail that check.

Navigation, input, screenshots, page reading, form filling and JavaScript run through Stagehand on cloud sessions; console and network reads rely on the plugin’s own listeners and page-injected tracking. update_plan only echoes the submitted plan, shortcuts return an empty list or a placeholder, and image upload and GIF export are placeholders. The author’s thread counts 19 extension tools; the reviewed dispatcher names 17.

The protocol account comes from the author’s X thread, not Anthropic documentation, and no captures or comparisons against the real extension are published. package.json declares Node test scripts, but the reviewed tree has no tests directory. This collection did not run the plugin, a cloud session or the extension; the undocumented local interface may change with Claude Code or extension updates.

README states MIT, but the reviewed tree has no LICENSE file and GitHub detects no license. Claude Code, the Claude in Chrome extension and Browserbase services keep their own terms, and browsed pages are processed on Browserbase infrastructure. The reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: Visor: an independent Ray-Ban Meta glasses client
description_en: Implements an Android replacement for the Meta AI companion app that speaks the Ray-Ban Meta glasses’ own Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct protocol, imports media, exposes settings and answers “Hey Meta” with a model the user chooses. The project wiki documents the link layers, encryption, services and Meta-side ownership steps, and lists 153 open questions. Testing is on real glasses rather than test suites, so behavior beyond the stated model and firmware remains unverified.
description_zh: 实现可替代 Meta AI 配套应用的 Android 客户端：直接使用 Ray-Ban Meta 眼镜自有的蓝牙与 Wi-Fi Direct 协议，导入媒体、提供设置，并用用户选择的模型回应“Hey Meta”。项目 wiki 记录了链路分层、加密、服务及 Meta 端的所有权流程，并列出 153 个未解问题。项目以实机试用代替测试套件，因此所述型号和固件之外的行为仍未经验证。
requirements: Reviewed just after release v1.3.1 (2026-10-18). README targets Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) tested on firmware 72387580077200100; other Meta glasses are untested. It needs an Android 10+ phone, a Meta account using password or email-code login (passkeys do not work) and, for the assistant, an Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible API key. The glasses accept one session at a time, so Visor and the Meta AI app displace each other.

Setup makes Visor the glasses’ owner app through Meta’s login and ownership-receipt services, so it still depends on a Meta account and Meta servers for setup, frame style and language packs. Source builds need three client tokens from the official Meta AI app, which the repository does not include; without them the app builds but login and ownership fail. Release builds read them from CI secrets.

Building needs JDK 21 and the Android SDK with platform 37. CI builds a debug APK with Gradle, and tagged releases publish a signed APK with a SHA-256 file; README lists the release certificate fingerprint. Modules separate wire format and ciphers, transport, session, identity, media, settings and the assistant, which stands in for Meta’s server with Claude or an OpenAI-compatible model.

There are no test suites: CONTRIBUTING asks for hardware trials and wire.log excerpts for protocol changes, and CLAUDE.md says the app works on real glasses as of 2026-10-05. The wiki marks unconfirmed facts and lists open questions, including unread payloads and model-specific values; CLAUDE.md also refers to a desktop Python client snapshot that the repository does not contain. This collection read source and documentation without running the app or glasses.

Visor is AGPL-3.0 and states it is unaffiliated with Meta or EssilorLuxottica; Meta’s services, app tokens, firmware and trademarks keep their own terms. CONTRIBUTING forbids getting unsigned software past the glasses’ signature checks. Claude is one selectable assistant backend, the repository’s CLAUDE.md is a contributor guide, and the reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: Super Mario Sunshine: a native PC port from an AI-assisted decompilation
description_en: Builds a native PC port of Super Mario Sunshine’s North American release from a pinned matching-decompilation fork, adding a host platform layer for graphics, disc, audio, input and OS services. The fork’s README says AI was used extensively to reconstruct and match its code; the port documents scripted regression hashes and lockstep comparisons with retail captures. Functions that do not yet match can still behave differently from retail, and the game must come from the user’s own disc image.
description_zh: 以固定版本的一致性反编译分支为基础，构建 Super Mario Sunshine 北美版的原生 PC 移植，并为图形、光盘、音频、输入和系统服务提供宿主平台层。该分支的 README 称，其代码的重建与匹配大量借助 AI；移植项目记录了脚本化回归哈希，以及与原版捕获数据的逐步对照。尚未匹配的函数仍可能与原版行为不同，游戏数据须来自使用者自己的光盘镜像。
requirements: Targets only the North American GMSE01 Rev 0 release. README reports the 32-bit Linux and macOS builds as playable, 64-bit Linux as playable but still being tested stage by stage, and 64-bit Windows as booting under Wine with native runtime checks. macOS builds x86_64, run under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon, because native arm64 cannot map game memory below 4 GiB.

Requires the user’s own GMSE01 Rev 0 disc image as .iso, .gcm or Dolphin .ciso; the port reads models, textures, levels, music and movies from it at run time and ships no game data. Given the image, the build also makes a standalone executable containing the game’s files, which README says must not be shared. Optional language, texture and HD-cutscene packs are separate.

build.sh and run.sh drive CMake, Python 3, patch, SDL2 and a host compiler: Ubuntu/Debian multilib GCC for the default 32-bit Linux build, Homebrew LLVM clang targeting x86_64 on macOS, or MSYS2 MINGW64 GCC on Windows. The decomp submodule is pinned to sms-english 967436b; PC-only changes are patches applied to copies of its sources, and the separate decomp build to a matching mario.dol uses its own GameCube toolchain.

At that pin, the fork’s PROGRESS.md reports, as of 2026-09-27, 99.57% fuzzy, 72.94% byte-perfect and 33.18% source-linked code, with 12,002 of 12,904 functions matching and a byte-identical rebuilt DOL that still links extracted objects for unfinished code; its README gives slightly higher 2026-09-29 figures. The port compiles the decomp’s 588 game, JSystem and THPPlayer units, so non-matching functions can still diverge from retail. It reports scripted headless runs hashed against a baseline and compared between 32- and 64-bit builds, lockstep tracing against retail Dolphin captures and qemu-ppc checks of math routines; this collection ran none of them.

The port is MIT-licensed (SoftwareAura LLC) and the decomp fork is CC0-1.0; the game and the user’s disc contents keep separate rights. AI involvement is stated by the fork’s README and agent guides, which describe Claude and Codex orchestrators, without measuring it; the reported X post adds no separate technical evidence. REA use is not established.

name: Majora’s Mask: matching US N64 decompilation
description_en: Recreates a C source base for The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask from information in the game and static or dynamic analysis, then rebuilds the US Nintendo 64 ROM. The build takes assets and assembly from a user-supplied ROM and checks the output against stored MD5 checksums. The team states it will not produce a PC port; the separately curated Zelda 64: Recompiled only credits it for headers and some functions.
description_zh: 依据游戏内信息和静态或动态分析，为《塞尔达传说：姆吉拉的假面》重建 C 源码库，并重新构建美版 Nintendo 64 ROM。构建流程从使用者自备的 ROM 中取得素材和汇编，再用仓库保存的 MD5 校验输出。团队声明不会制作 PC 移植；另行收录的 Zelda 64: Recompiled 只注明借用了其头文件和部分函数。
requirements: README calls this a work-in-progress decompilation whose codebase may still change drastically, and warns that some parts of the ROM may not yet be shiftable, so modifications can be difficult. Only N64 US 1.0 is supported; the Makefile also lists a WIP N64 Japan 1.1 target with checksum comparison disabled. Majora’s Mask 3D is out of scope, and the output is an N64 ROM, not a PC executable.

Supply your own US Majora’s Mask ROM as the base ROM; .z64, .n64 and .v64 byte orders are accepted. The repository includes no game assets or assembly: the build decompresses the supplied ROM and derives files, assets and disassembled code and data from it before compiling a ROM and a compressed ROM.

The documented host is Linux, native or under WSL or a VM, with Debian or Ubuntu recommended: Git, build-essential, MIPS binutils, curl, Python 3 with pip and venv, libpng and libxml2. macOS and Docker have separate guides. The default compiler is a static recompilation of IDO 5.3 and 7.1 that the tools Makefile downloads from decompals/ido-static-recomp; GCC and NON_MATCHING builds turn the checksum comparison off.

A default build checks both ROMs against stored MD5 values and prints OK or FAILED; FAILED means a bad base ROM or non-matching code. CI builds the US version in matching mode and Japan 1.1 as non-matching, using base ROMs from the project’s build container. The project’s mutable progress badge read 100% at review while the README still says WIP; this collection did not rerun the build.

The reviewed tree has no top-level license file and GitHub detects no license, so source reuse terms are unstated; ROM contents and derived assets keep their own rights. The README forbids contributions from anyone who has ever accessed leaked Nintendo 64 SDK, libultra or Zelda 64 source. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: wine-uwp: running packaged Windows Store apps on a patched Wine
description_en: Extends Wine 11.17 so that signed MSIX Store apps, with Shapr3D as the main target, install and run on Linux without their source or symbols. About 49,000 changed lines add a DirectComposition implementation, composition swap chains and an app-model host, while Microsoft’s own XAML and app-model DLLs, harvested from a Windows 11 image on the user’s machine, run unmodified. The author says Claude did most of the reverse engineering and code; app support is uneven and checked by a project regression suite.
description_zh: 扩展 Wine 11.17，使已签名的 MSIX 商店应用（主要目标为 Shapr3D）无需源码或符号即可在 Linux 上安装运行。约 49,000 行改动新增了 DirectComposition 实现、合成交换链和应用模型宿主；微软自己的 XAML 与应用模型 DLL 则在使用者机器上从 Windows 11 镜像中提取后原样运行。作者称大部分逆向工程和代码由 Claude 完成；各应用支持程度不一，由项目回归测试检查。
requirements: README’s app table reports Shapr3D sketching, modelling, menus, cloud sync, sign-in and STL/PDF export; Solitaire playable; Media Player playing audio from its own UI; Calculator fully working; Feedback Hub interactive; and Camera only reaching its own error page. Shapr3D for Linux (58d9173) packages this same pinned wine-uwp commit as a beta AppImage and Flatpak; it is unofficial and not affiliated with Shapr3D.

Needs the user’s own app package (.msix or .msixbundle, or Shapr3D’s .appinstaller, from which setup downloads about 1.8 GB) and Windows components extracted from Microsoft’s free Windows 11 evaluation ISO or another Windows 11 image. Neither the repositories nor the release packages contain them, and a commit hook refuses Windows binaries. Shapr3D also needs an account and a browser sign-in.

Building copies the vendored wine/ files over the Wine 11.17 source, then runs autoreconf, configure with --enable-archs=x86_64 and make; the WinRT stand-in shims build with clang-cl and lld-link against Windows SDK headers fetched by xwin. Shapr3D for Linux needs 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.38+, working Vulkan drivers and about 11 GB free during setup, and its releases build with flatpak-builder on the freedesktop 25.08 SDK.

regress.sh requires Calculator to stay pixel-identical to a committed baseline and other apps to come up on a private Xvfb display; release.sh smoke-tests that an empty setup reaches Shapr3D’s first screen. The Findings logs record failed approaches as well as fixes. These checks are project-reported; this collection did not build Wine or run any app.

Neither repository has a top-level license file, and GitHub detects none. The vendored Wine files carry LGPL-2.1-or-later headers and the setup app’s Cargo manifest declares the same; the shims and investigation tools state no license. Harvested Microsoft components and Store apps keep their own terms, and the plan notes that a distributable product would need clean-room replacements for them. The author’s X posts disclose heavy Claude assistance; REA use is not established.

name: DLSSNR-AMD: reimplementing DLSS 5 neural rendering for RDNA4
description_en: Reimplements the neural-rendering network of NVIDIA’s DLSS 5 library as Vulkan compute shaders for AMD RX 9000 (RDNA4) cards and supplies it to games through an NGX-compatible core and ReShade or Vulkan-layer routes. The weights are not distributed: installers extract them, hash-checked, from the user’s own nvngx_dlssnr.dll 310.9.16 or 310.8.0. The project compares its output with NVIDIA’s DLL on an RTX 5090 and reports close, not bit-identical, pictures.
description_zh: 将 NVIDIA DLSS 5 库中的神经渲染网络重新实现为面向 AMD RX 9000（RDNA4）显卡的 Vulkan 计算着色器，并通过兼容 NGX 的核心模块以及 ReShade 或 Vulkan 层等途径提供给游戏。项目不分发权重：安装程序从使用者自己的 nvngx_dlssnr.dll 310.9.16 或 310.8.0 中提取权重并核对哈希。项目将输出与 NVIDIA DLL 在 RTX 5090 上的结果对比，报告画面接近但并非逐位一致。
requirements: The reviewed 0.0.x main targets RX 9000 cards because the network needs RDNA4 FP8 matrix instructions, reached through VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix; README says it was tested only on an RX 9070 XT. Linux under Steam/Proton with Mesa 26.2+ is the main version; Windows is an experimental preview tested with AMD Software 26.9.2, slower by default and closer to Linux with precompiled ACO machine code. OpenGL games are unsupported, and README warns against online games with anti-cheat.

Requires the user’s own nvngx_dlssnr.dll, version 310.9.16 (both models) or 310.8.0 (the old model only); other versions are refused, and a model file is written only when every extracted entry matches a known hash. README says packages containing the model must not be shared. The optional int4-mixed network derives its weights at install from the user’s model and project calibration tables, which THIRD_PARTY.md says hold no weight values.

The documented build runs on Ubuntu 24.04 with git, curl, Python 3, CMake, Ninja, MinGW-w64 and multilib g++; fetch_deps.sh pins third-party components, including glslang 16.5.0 for reproducible SPIR-V, and the Windows DLLs are cross-compiled. Games reach the network through an NGX core loaded by OptiScaler-NR, for DirectX 11/12 titles with an upscaler option, or through ReShade-based routes that estimate motion from the picture.

For the 310.9.16 model, the verification notes report single-frame PSNR of 49.15–50.59 dB and SSIM of about 0.997 against NVIDIA’s unmodified DLL on an RTX 5090, plus short moving sequences, from one Tomb Raider (2013) frame and its downscales; the 310.8.0 comparison reports 45.56–49.06 dB. These are project measurements on one AMD card; this collection ran neither side.

MIT covers the repository’s code; third-party components keep their own licenses, including GPL-3.0 OptiScaler-NR shipped as released. NVIDIA’s DLL and weights remain NVIDIA’s, and the project states it is not affiliated with NVIDIA or AMD. The repository does not describe how the network structure was recovered; its CLAUDE.md addresses coding assistants but does not establish AI authorship. REA use is not established.

name: Breath of the Wild: per-function matching decompilation of the Switch executable
description_en: Reimplements part of Breath of the Wild’s Switch v1.5.0 main executable in C++ and checks each function against the original machine code. The project calls itself a hybrid decompilation/reimplementation: it contains no assets, its ELF holds only reimplemented functions and cannot run the game, and porting is an explicit non-goal.
description_zh: 以 C++ 重新实现《塞尔达传说 旷野之息》Switch v1.5.0 主程序的部分代码，并逐个函数与原始机器码比对。项目自称是反编译与重新实现的混合体：不含游戏素材，生成的 ELF 仅包含已重新实现的函数、无法运行游戏，移植到其他平台也明确不是目标。
requirements: README calls this an experimental work-in-progress decompilation of Switch v1.5.0. The About page scopes it to the main executable (game code and most statically linked libraries), excluding RomFS assets, dynamically linked SDK libraries, libcurl, NEX and most of Havok. Functions are matched individually rather than placed at original addresses, so this is not a whole-executable matching build, a playable game or a port.

Setup needs the user’s own main NSO executable from the Switch release. The pinned setup script verifies its hash, uses 1.5.0 directly and converts listed 1.6.0 or 1.9.0 executables to 1.5.0 with a project-hosted patch; RomFS and other game content are not used. The About page says the project is useless to anyone who does not own the game.

The installation guide assumes Linux (native or WSL) or macOS and lists Python 3, Ninja, CMake, ccache, xdelta3, Clang and a Rust toolchain; the pinned CMakeLists requires CMake 3.30. Setup fetches Clang 4.0.1 for game code and installs tools/check. Submodules supply sead, agl, EventFlow, NintendoSDK headers and the shared nx-decomp-tools; the decompiling guide works from Hex-Rays or Ghidra output.

tools/check diffs each listed function against the original executable, and data/uking_functions.csv records its status. At the pinned commit that list marks 32,079 of 113,490 functions matching, 514 non-matching, 7,601 work in progress, 6,270 library and 67,026 not decompiled; the mutable botw.link badges showed 17.493% by size and 30.398% by function on review. This collection did not run the checker.

The pinned tree has no root license file and GitHub detects none, so no reuse license is stated; submodules and Nintendo content keep their own terms, and the About page calls the work a legal gray zone. AGENTS.md sets disclosure and human-review rules for AI-assisted contributions, but the reviewed files neither attribute the reconstruction to REA nor quantify AI use.

name: Skyward Sword: Wii decompilation with hash-checked relinking
description_en: Reconstructs C++ source for The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword’s Wii main.dol and REL modules, starting from the user’s NTSC-U 1.0 (SOUE01) disc files. Objects marked matching are compiled from source and linked with objects split from the original, and the result is checked against SHA-1 hashes; the repository ships no assets or assembly and is not a port.
description_zh: 以使用者自备的 NTSC-U 1.0（SOUE01）光盘文件为起点，为《塞尔达传说 天空之剑》Wii 版的 main.dol 和 REL 模块重建 C++ 源码。标为一致的对象由源码编译，再与从原文件拆分出的其余对象链接，并以 SHA-1 哈希校验结果；仓库不含素材或汇编，也不是移植。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress Wii decompilation whose only supported version is SOUE01 (NTSC-U 1.0); configure.py also lists SOUP01, but the pinned tree has configuration only for SOUE01. The output is a rebuilt main.dol and REL set for the Wii, not a PC executable or port.

Building needs the user’s own SOUE01 game: README names sys/main.dol and files/rels.arc from its data partition as the only required files. The repository contains no game assets or assembly; decomp-toolkit splits the user’s files into objects locally, using the input hash and split tables in config/SOUE01.

Builds run natively on Windows with Python and ninja, or on Linux/macOS with ninja and the automatically downloaded wibo wrapper. configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.7.1, objdiff v3.4.1, binutils 2.42-1 and a 20250812 compiler bundle, selecting Metrowerks Wii/1.5 for most code and Wii/1.3 for most NW4R code; objdiff compares individual objects during development.

The default ninja target links source-built objects only for units marked Matching (493 in configure.py; 536 remain NonMatching) and uses the original extracted object for the rest, then checks main.dol and 636 RELs against build.sha1. A passing check shows output identity, not complete decompilation. decomp.dev’s report for the pinned commit lists 27.89% of code bytes and 33,940 of 76,968 functions matched; CI uses a private container holding game files, and this collection ran neither.
The repository carries CC0-1.0; that dedication does not cover Nintendo’s game, its files or the downloaded compilers. The reviewed sources establish no REA or coding-agent involvement.
